blocks.explanation:
Pehle series ko ghaur se dekhiye: 3, 6, 9, ... har term pichhli se 3 zyada hai. Jab har dafa same number jud raha ho to yeh arithmetic series (A.P. ka jama) hoti hai.
Diya kya hai? Pehli term 3 aur aakhri term \(a_{20}\), yani kul 20 terms.
Find kya karna hai? In 20 terms ka jama \(S_{20}\).
Plan: pehle \(d\), phir aakhri term \(a_{20}\), aur phir \(S_n = \frac{n}{2}(a_1 + a_n)\) wala formula.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(3 + 6 + 9 + \dots + a_{20}\).
Humein find karna hai: 20 terms ka jama \(S_{20}\).
Tareeqa: Terms barabar barabar barh rahi hain, is liye yeh arithmetic series hai. Jab pehli aur aakhri term dono maloom hon to \(S_n = \frac{n}{2}(a_1 + a_n)\) sab se chhota raasta hai. Aakhri term abhi number mein nahi di, is liye pehle usay \(a_n\) ke formula se nikalenge.

Common difference nikalein
\[d = 6 - 3 = 3\]
\[9 - 6 = 3 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: A.P. mein kisi bhi term mein se us se pehli term minus karein to hamesha wohi number \(d\) aata hai. Hum ne do jagah check kiya taake yaqeen ho jaye ke series waqai A.P. hai.

Aakhri term \(a_{20}\) nikalein
\[a_n = a_1 + (n - 1)d\]
\[a_{20} = 3 + 19(3)\]
\[= 3 + 57 = 60\]
Kyun: Pehli term se 20th term tak pahunchne ke liye 19 qadam chalne parte hain, aur har qadam \(d = 3\) ka hai. Is liye \(3 + 19 \times 3\).
Dhyan dein: Bahut se students \(20 \times 3\) jor dete hain; qadam hamesha \(n - 1\) hote hain, \(n\) nahi.

Jama ka formula lagayein
\[S_n = \dfrac{n}{2}(a_1 + a_n)\]
\[S_{20} = \dfrac{20}{2}(3 + 60)\]
\[= 10 \times 63 = 630\]
Kyun: Yeh formula kehta hai: terms ki tadaad ka aadha, pehli aur aakhri term ke jama se multiply. Is ka raaz yeh hai ke A.P. mein pehli + aakhri, doosri + doosri-aakhri, sab jore barabar hote hain (yahan har jora 63), aur kul 10 jore bante hain.

Tasdeeq: doosre formula se
\[S_{20} = \dfrac{20}{2}[2(3) + 19(3)]\]
\[= 10(6 + 57) = 630 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: \(S_n = \frac{n}{2}[2a_1 + (n-1)d]\) bhi wohi jawab de raha hai, to hamara jawab pakka hai. Ek aur aasaan tasdeeq: \(3 + 6 + \dots + 60 = 3(1 + 2 + \dots + 20) = 3 \times 210 = 630\).
blocks.final_answer:
\(S_{20} = 630\)
Yani 3 se 60 tak 3 ke pehle 20 multiples ka jama 630 hai.

blocks.explanation:
Is series mein surds (jaise \(\sqrt{5}\), jinka exact jawab decimal mein khatam nahi hota) hain, is liye pehli nazar mein pattern nazar nahi aata. Trick yeh hai ke \(\sqrt{5}\) ko bhi \(\sqrt{5}\) ke neeche likh dein.
Diya kya hai? Pehli teen terms aur aakhri term \(a_n\).
Find kya karna hai? \(n\) terms ka jama \(S_n\), jo \(n\) ki shakal mein aayega.
Plan: sab terms ek hi denominator par, \(a_1\) aur \(d\) nikalna, phir \(S_n = \frac{n}{2}[2a_1 + (n-1)d]\).
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(\frac{4}{\sqrt{5}} + \sqrt{5} + \frac{6}{\sqrt{5}} + \dots + a_n\).
Humein find karna hai: \(S_n\), yani \(n\) terms ka jama.
Tareeqa: Har term ko \(\sqrt{5}\) ke denominator par likh kar common difference dekhenge. Kyunke yahan \(n\) koi number nahi balke letter hai aur aakhri term ki value bhi nahi di, is liye \(S_n = \frac{n}{2}[2a_1 + (n-1)d]\) use karenge jis mein sirf \(a_1\), \(d\) aur \(n\) chahiye.

\(\sqrt{5}\) ko \(\sqrt{5}\) ke neeche likhein
\[\sqrt{5} = \dfrac{\sqrt{5} \cdot \sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{5}} = \dfrac{5}{\sqrt{5}}\]
Series: \(\frac{4}{\sqrt{5}} + \frac{5}{\sqrt{5}} + \frac{6}{\sqrt{5}} + \dots\)
Kyun: Kisi number ko upar neeche same cheez se multiply karein to value nahi badalti. \(\sqrt{5} \cdot \sqrt{5} = 5\) hota hai, is liye \(\sqrt{5} = \frac{5}{\sqrt{5}}\). Ab upar 4, 5, 6 hain jo saaf 1, 1 barh rahe hain; pattern khul kar saamne aa gaya.

\(a_1\) aur \(d\) nikalein
\[a_1 = \dfrac{4}{\sqrt{5}}\]
\[d = \dfrac{5}{\sqrt{5}} - \dfrac{4}{\sqrt{5}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\]
Kyun: \(d\) hamesha doosri term minus pehli term. Teesri se doosri minus karein to bhi \(\frac{6}{\sqrt{5}} - \frac{5}{\sqrt{5}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\) aata hai, to series pakki A.P. hai.
Dhyan dein: \(d\) ko \(\sqrt{5} - \frac{4}{\sqrt{5}}\) seedha nikalne mein ghalti ho jati hai; pehle same denominator par le aana sab se mehfooz hai.

Jama ka formula lagayein
\[S_n = \dfrac{n}{2}[2a_1 + (n - 1)d]\]
\[= \dfrac{n}{2}\left[\dfrac{8}{\sqrt{5}} + \dfrac{n - 1}{\sqrt{5}}\right]\]
Kyun: \(2a_1 = 2 \times \frac{4}{\sqrt{5}} = \frac{8}{\sqrt{5}}\), aur \((n - 1)d = (n - 1) \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} = \frac{n - 1}{\sqrt{5}}\). Bas values formula mein rakh di hain.

Simplify karein
\[S_n = \dfrac{n}{2} \cdot \dfrac{8 + n - 1}{\sqrt{5}}\]
\[= \dfrac{n(n + 7)}{2\sqrt{5}}\]
Kyun: Bracket ke andar dono fractions ka denominator \(\sqrt{5}\) hai, is liye sirf upar wale jor diye: \(8 + n - 1 = n + 7\). Phir \(\frac{n}{2}\) se multiply kiya. Agar chahein to upar neeche \(\sqrt{5}\) se multiply kar ke \(\frac{\sqrt{5}\,n(n + 7)}{10}\) bhi likh sakte hain; dono barabar hain.

Tasdeeq: \(n = 3\) rakh kar
\[\dfrac{4 + 5 + 6}{\sqrt{5}} = \dfrac{15}{\sqrt{5}}\]
\[\dfrac{3(3 + 7)}{2\sqrt{5}} = \dfrac{30}{2\sqrt{5}} = \dfrac{15}{\sqrt{5}} \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Jab jawab \(n\) ki shakal mein ho to kisi chhote \(n\) ke liye haath se jama kar ke formula se milana sab se achhi tasdeeq hai. Pehli teen terms ka jama aur formula dono \(\frac{15}{\sqrt{5}}\) de rahe hain.
blocks.final_answer:
\(S_n = \frac{n(n + 7)}{2\sqrt{5}}\) (yahi \(\frac{\sqrt{5}\,n(n + 7)}{10}\) bhi hai)
Answer key bhi \(\frac{n(n + 7)}{2\sqrt{5}}\) deti hai.
